items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: Then we had Paul -- Paul Jones played tenor sax. Peter Pole played alto sax.

ctx.x: I don't think nobody would know many of the guys, but I'd like to tell you, this was just one trombone, myself. And then we had a trumpet player named Daniel Brashier -- Georgetown we called because he lived in the Georgetown section. And we had another trumpet player from down South, Jake. I can't think of -- he was from North Carolina, but Jake died. And that's what was the brass, two trumpets and a trombone.

Then we had Paul -- Paul Jones played tenor sax. Peter Pole played alto sax. There was another alto man. I can't think of his name. We had three saxes and two trumpets and one trombone. Then we had Jimmy Holmes was the guitar player. And then -- he's the guy I told you who died. He was a left hand guitar player -- violin and guitar. Fantastic player.

But none of them -- Booker Coleman was the leader. He played piano, and he was the leader. And we had a guy named Moody was the drummer. And that was it. We had two trumpets, a trombone, three saxophones, and we had a piano, drums. And that was a big band for those times, you know. And bass. And the bass player's name was Carrington.
